\chapter{Witnesses and oaths}
\label{ch:ar-witnesses-and-oaths}
\hlchaptermodality{325}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say to witness, to swear, to take an oath, to confess and to deny.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 325: I can say to witness, to swear, to take an oath, to confess and to deny.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{شهد} (shahida)}{شهد (shahida)}]{\ar{شهد} (shahida) — to witness; to testify}

\label{lesson:AR-C325-shahida}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a whistle, then the Arabic for chaos.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{شهد}}
\textbf{\ar{شهد}} — \emph{shahida} — \textquotedblleft{}to witness; to testify\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{شهدت} \ar{المدينة} \ar{مطرا} \ar{شديدا} \ar{أمس}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shahidat al-madīna maṭaran shadīdan ams.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The city saw heavy rain yesterday.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يشهد}, \emph{yashhad}.

\ar{شهد} \ar{على} or \ar{شهد} \ar{بـ}: to testify. A witness is \ar{شاهد}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{شهد}} (\emph{shahida}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-h-d} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to be present at a thing and see it\textquotedblright{}; \emph{shahāda} is testimony, and a certificate.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shahida}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shahida}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shahidat al-madīna maṭaran shadīdan ams.} — The city saw heavy rain yesterday.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a whistle, then the Arabic for chaos, then say \emph{shahida} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{شهد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To witness; to testify\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أقسم} (aqsama)}{أقسم (aqsama)}]{\ar{أقسم} (aqsama) — to swear}

\label{lesson:AR-C325-aqsama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for chaos, then the Arabic for to witness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أقسم}}
\textbf{\ar{أقسم}} — \emph{aqsama} — \textquotedblleft{}to swear\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أقسم} \ar{الشاهد} \ar{أن} \ar{كلامه} \ar{صحيح}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aqsama ash-shāhid anna kalāmahu ṣaḥīḥ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The witness swore that what he said was true.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يقسم}, \emph{yuqsim}.

The oath itself is \ar{قسم}, \emph{qasam}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أقسم}} (\emph{aqsama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-s-m} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to divide\textquotedblright{}, the root of \emph{qism}, a part. Lane gives \emph{qasam} as an oath, and Form IV \emph{aqsama}, to swear.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aqsama}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aqsama}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aqsama ash-shāhid anna kalāmahu ṣaḥīḥ.} — The witness swore that what he said was true.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for chaos, then the Arabic for to witness, then say \emph{aqsama} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أقسم} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To swear\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حلف} (ḥalafa)}{حلف (ḥalafa)}]{\ar{حلف} (ḥalafa) — to take an oath}

\label{lesson:AR-C325-halafa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to witness, then the Arabic for to swear.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حلف}}
\textbf{\ar{حلف}} — \emph{ḥalafa} — \textquotedblleft{}to take an oath\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حلف} \ar{الموظف} \ar{أمام} \ar{المحكمة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥalafa al-muwaẓẓaf amāma al-maḥkama.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The employee took an oath before the court.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يحلف}, \emph{yaḥlif}.

An ally, one bound by oath, is \ar{حليف}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حلف}} (\emph{ḥalafa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-l-f} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to swear\textquotedblright{}; \emph{ḥilf} is a pact sworn between tribes, and \emph{ḥalīf} an ally.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥalafa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥalafa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥalafa al-muwaẓẓaf amāma al-maḥkama.} — The employee took an oath before the court.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to witness, then the Arabic for to swear, then say \emph{ḥalafa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{حلف} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To take an oath\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اعترف} (iʿtarafa)}{اعترف (iʿtarafa)}]{\ar{اعترف} (iʿtarafa) — to confess, to admit}

\label{lesson:AR-C325-itarafa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to swear, then the Arabic for to take an oath.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اعترف}}
\textbf{\ar{اعترف}} — \emph{iʿtarafa} — \textquotedblleft{}to confess, to admit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اعترف} \ar{اللص} \ar{بالسرقة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{iʿtarafa al-liṣṣ bi-s-sariqa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The thief confessed to the theft.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يعترف}, \emph{yaʿtarif}.

It takes \ar{بـ}: \ar{اعترف} \ar{بالخطأ}, he admitted the mistake.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اعترف}} (\emph{iʿtarafa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-r-f} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to know\textquotedblright{}, the root of the taught \emph{ʿarafa}. It is Form VIII, \textquotedblleft{}to own that one knows\textquotedblright{}: to admit.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iʿtarafa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iʿtarafa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iʿtarafa al-liṣṣ bi-s-sariqa.} — The thief confessed to the theft.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to swear, then the Arabic for to take an oath, then say \emph{iʿtarafa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{اعترف} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To confess, to admit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أنكر} (ankara)}{أنكر (ankara)}]{\ar{أنكر} (ankara) — to deny}

\label{lesson:AR-C325-ankara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to take an oath, then the Arabic for to confess.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أنكر}}
\textbf{\ar{أنكر}} — \emph{ankara} — \textquotedblleft{}to deny\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أنكر} \ar{المتهم} \ar{كل} \ar{شيء}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ankara al-muttaham kull shayʾ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The defendant denied everything.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينكر}, \emph{yunkir}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أنكر}} (\emph{ankara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-k-r} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}not to know a thing\textquotedblright{}; \emph{nakira} is \textquotedblleft{}to find strange\textquotedblright{}. It is Form IV, \textquotedblleft{}to disown\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ankara}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ankara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ankara al-muttaham kull shayʾ.} — The defendant denied everything.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to take an oath, then the Arabic for to confess, then say \emph{ankara} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
